Consult Summary:
34-year-old woman with 3-day history of profuse watery→loose diarrhoea, vomiting, feverish sensation, and periumbilical abdominal pain; likely infectious gastroenteritis. Advised continued oral rehydration, simple diet, stool sample and hydration review in urgent clinic; attend A&E if deterioration.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute diarrhoea and vomiting
- Onset: 3 days ago; initially watery, now very loose; “lost count” of episodes, ≥4 today.
- Associated symptoms: Recurrent vomiting (unable to tolerate water/tea/ORS), subjective fever (“literally boiling”), periumbilical cramping pain precipitating urge to defecate; no blood in stool or urine; last vomit 2 h ago.
- Contact history: Brother and “everyone in school” with similar symptoms.
- Review of systems: No rash; normal baseline bowel habit (once daily); able to pass urine (last 1 h ago, colour unobserved).
- Impression: Probable infectious gastroenteritis (viral vs bacterial). Differential includes food-borne bacterial infection.

Issue 2: Risk of dehydration
- Vomiting all oral intake; relying on oral rehydration salts (ORS) 3×/day for 2 days.
- Passed urine recently (positive sign) but still at risk; needs clinical assessment of hydration.

Issue 3: Abdominal pain
- Localised around umbilicus, soreness to touch, intermittent, correlates with bowel motion.
- No prior abdominal pathology; no recent surgery.

Medications:
- Vitamin D supplement – dose/route/frequency not documented (taken daily).
- Ibuprofen PRN for dysmenorrhoea – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Oral rehydration salts (ORS) – approx. 3 times daily for past 2 days.

Allergies:
- Not documented. (missing)

Past Medical History:
- Generally well; history of occasional menstrual cramps. No previous abdominal disease or surgery.

Social History:
- Lives with mother and brother.
- Occupation: Graphic designer; currently working from home due to illness.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Occasional pint.
- No recreational drug use.
- Not sexually active; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; not on contraception.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Remote consult; no vitals recorded.
- Subjective feverishness reported.
- No skin rash per patient.

Plan:
- Arrange urgent in-clinic appointment for:
  • Stool sample for microscopy/culture to rule out bacterial pathogens.
  • Clinical assessment of hydration status.
- Continue oral rehydration salts: frequent tiny sips to improve tolerance.
- Diet: bland/light foods (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk.
- Safety-net:
  • Call service or attend A&E urgently if worsening vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, reduced urine output, high fever, blood in stool, or increasing abdominal pain.
- Patient to book appointment via support line ASAP.
- Monitor symptoms; follow-up once stool results available or sooner if condition changes.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: allergy status, current temperature, weight, recent travel/food history detail, medication reconciliation confirmation, baseline vitals.
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.
● Transcript quality: clear; occasional minor inaudible/overlapping speech but clinically adequate.
